result.title: Different Timescales, Different Signals: Multimodal Landmark-Visibility Prediction in a Long-Term Webcam Network
result.comment: 18 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables. Accepted to the MM4SciReal Workshop at ACCV 2026
result.summary: Scenic visibility is not a single forecasting problem: planning a trip months ahead, deciding whether to go outside today, and judging whether tomorrow will be clear rely on different information. Using a year-scale multimodal archive of Mount Fuji webcams and meteorological observations, we identify a clear hierarchy across timescales. Seasonal climatology provides useful long-range guidance, webcam imagery is the strongest same-day observation (AUC 0.95), and the numerical forecast valid on the target day carries most of the day-specific signal one to three days ahead. Revealing this hierarchy requires evaluation that respects the dependence among cameras observing the same regional weather state: permissive splits substantially overstate multi-day performance, while date-grouped and forward-in-time evaluation reduce the apparent contribution of the current scene and current weather. On 6,575 camera-days, the current visual summary provides no measurable one-day gain once the target-day forecast is available. The remaining opportunity lies at shorter horizons, where the present visual representation discards cloud geometry and motion. These results recast scenic visibility prediction as a multi-timescale sensing problem rather than a single multimodal forecasting task.

AI.brief_summary: 论文利用一年期的富士山网络摄像头与气象观测档案，比较季节气候、当日图像与目标日数值预报在不同预报时程上对能见度预测的贡献，并比较按日期分组、前向时间等切分方式对评估结论的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按时间尺度拆解并量化「当前视觉证据」增益的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉信息是否被真正使用及贡献分配，而「目标日预报可用时视觉无增益」与现有表示丢失云几何和运动，也与视觉旁路和信息坍缩问题相似。
